card.name: Words explaining where cases or excretion occur
card.fires_on: Words that complete a phrase about where, when or how something happened or is eliminated, such as 'cases occurred', 'excreted in the feces', or 'acquired in the hospital'. It also fires on a preposition or comma right after a count of cases.

modes.label: Cases occurred
modes.description: The verb or link after 'reported cases' or 'half of the cases', before a time or setting.
modes.example: Approximately half of the reported cases<< occurred>> within the initial 3 months of treatment

modes.label: Excretion route
modes.description: Words ending a route-of-elimination phrase, such as feces, renally, or biliary system.
modes.example: Since the metabolites and the unchanged drug are mainly excreted in the fec<<es>>, no dosage adjustment is required for patients

modes.label: Source or origin preposition
modes.description: A preposition after a share or amount saying where it came from or was acquired.
modes.example: No more than 25% of cases of Clostridium difficile in hospitals are actually acquired<< in>> the hospital, a three-hospital study

card.writes: The promoted and suppressed tokens are mixed and unrelated, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It lights up on words that say where, when, or by what route something happened, like cases occurring or a drug being excreted.
